{{Quote|Messy and imprecise. The lanvarok is a weapon of indiscriminate terror.|Darth Sidious|<ref name="BOS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref>}}
The '''lanvarok''' was a combination two-handed polearm weapon and projectile launcher that released sharp, [[Poison/Legends|poison]]-coated discs guided by the power of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]]. Initially purposed as a [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]] tool, the massive lanvarok was the primary combat weapon of the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors of the [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]] [[Species/Legends|species]], both melee and ranged, and also the device brandished by [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] during ceremonies. The [[Massassi lanvarok|original lanvarok]] was inspired by the natural left-[[Limb/Legends|handed]] disposition of all members of the Sith species, a distinction that was also maintained in the weapon's [[Sith lanvarok|alternate forearm-mounted, combat-exclusive projectile dispenser]] design. A right-handed version was later developed by [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lords]] of [[Human/Legends|Human]] descent.

Prevalent during the ancient [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]], use of lanvaroks was confined to the borders of [[Sith Worlds/Legends|Sith space]] until they were exposed to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] by the Massassi who fought on behalf of the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. Lanvaroks were brought to the jungle [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] by the warriors who joined Sadow in [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]], and remained the foremost weapon of the Massassi for more than a [[3997 BBY|thousand years]]. A variant of the lanvarok was later developed as a forearm-mounted gauntlet. Both versions were especially uncommon in the galaxy at large after the extinction of the Sith race, although an occasional lanvarok was found among the collections of antique dealers, the cargoes of [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]], or the arsenals of [[Assassin/Legends|assassins]]. Those Massassi warriors who served aboard the [[Sith dreadnaught]] [[Harbinger (Sith dreadnaught)|''Harbinger'']] that was propelled [[41 ABY|five thousand years]] forward in [[Time/Legends|time]] brought lanvaroks with them into the modern era.

==Description==
===Battleaxe===
{{Main|Massassi lanvarok}}
{{Listen3|Lanvarok1-DLOTS.flac|A lanvarok disc in flight}}
The original lanvarok, fabricated at a cost of about 250 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]],<ref name="KOTORCG" /> was a large polearm weapon that was at least as tall as the [[Sentience/Legends|beings]] for whom it was designed, the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors of the ancient [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]],<ref name="DLOTS4" /> a [[Species/Legends|species]] whose inherent left-handed predilection was the weapon's inspiration.<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> Prior to their discovery of [[Metallurgy/Legends|metallurgy]] and the manipulation of alloys thereby derived, materials such as [[Wood/Legends|wood]] and [[Bone/Legends|bone]] were used in the construction of lanvaroks and the discs with which it was equipped.<ref name="NEGWT" /> Sharply speared at either end, the exotic lanvarok included a compact, crescent-shaped axehead at its summit with an opposing long spike,<ref name="DSS" /> a shape reminiscent to some of a [[Dreadnaught/Legends|dreadnaught]] [[Warship/Legends|warship]].<ref name="CC" /> Several small, [[Poison/Legends|poison]]-coated discs valued at five credits apiece<ref name="KOTORCG" /> were spring-loaded and hidden within a launcher mounted on the side of the axehead.<ref name="NEGWT" /> The heft of the weapon, at just under ten [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]],<ref name="KOTORCG" /> was such that only the especially strong Massassi warrior was capable of using it effectively.<ref name="CC" /> Individuals occasionally decorated their personal weapons with tassels<ref name="DLOTS4" /> and inscriptions.<ref name="NEGWT" />

===Variant===
{{Main|Sith lanvarok}}
{{Quote|Oh my, a Sith lanvarok, and it's in exquisite condition. [&hellip;] You know I'll pay your price.|Plumba, to the proprietor of Antiques by Dumas|<ref name="MR4" />}}
[[File:LanvarokSchematic.jpg|thumb|left|270px|A Sith lanvarok schematic]]
The battleaxe version of the lanvarok was adapted into a forearm-mounted gauntlet<ref name="BOS" /> that bore few similarities to the original, including an inflated 4,000 credit price tag.<ref name="KOTORCG" /> Forged of [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] and sometimes plated with [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]]-impervious [[Cortosis/Legends|cortosis]] alloy,<ref name="NEGWT" /> the gauntlet model was lighter,<ref name="KOTORCG" /> and was not a halberd with ranged attack capabilities granted by an equipped disc launcher, but was instead a worn device similar in function to a [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]]. A thick, perforated and padded metal cuff around the base of the forearm supported the attached launcher mechanism, disc cartridge, and emitter. The channel through which the ejected disc traveled extended from the launcher assembly and tapered at the end of the user's hand, and included a primary triggering handle that curved downward and fit into the wielder's grip. An additional release trigger was installed near the underside of the forearm cuff and required [[The Force/Legends|Force]]-manipulation to subtly activate the disc launcher.<ref name="NEGWT" /> Among the design cues that were transferred to the new lanvarok were the weapon's left-handed exclusivity. However, further modifications saw the development of a right-handed version<ref name="END" /> which, like those specifically suited to left-handed warriors, was not interchangeable from either side.<ref name="DSS" />

===Usage===
{{Quote|Primitive weaponry&hellip;but accurate!|Exar Kun|audio=Lanvarok2-DLOTS.flac|<ref name="Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio)">[[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith'' audio drama]]</ref>}}
Brute strength rather than skill was necessary to properly control the massive lanvarok,<ref name="NEGWT" /> in a firm two-handed grip, with one hand at the base of the [[Hilt/Legends|hilt]] and the other situated underneath the axehead.<ref name="DLOTS4" /> A quick forward swing and return of the weapon released a single poison-coated disc, while a longer arc cast a wider flurry of multiple discs which were aimed at the [[Throat/Legends|throat]] and face,<ref name="CC" /> but instead fanned out in a wildly random pattern.<ref name="NEGWT" /> Because of their unpredictable trajectory, Massassi sometimes guided the discs with [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] power to targets as distant as five [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="DSS" /> with such precision as to even disarm opponents.<ref name="DLOTS4" /> Sith Lords, for whom the weapon was not designed, only carried lanvaroks during ceremony and were compelled to direct its discs through the Force. When the lanvarok had exhausted its ammunition, which was time-consuming to reload, the axehead became the primary means of attack. The curved shape of the blade easily penetrated scaled [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] hides, and was ideal for rending flesh from bone, as well as the clean removal of [[Limb/Legends|limbs]] and heads. The long, sharp opposite end was speared through targets in a [[Death/Legends|killing]] maneuver.<ref name="NEGWT" />

Defensively, Massassi lanvaroks were held aloft to parry incoming attacks. In an intimidating gesture, adept warriors spun their weapons with sufficient speed to produce an audible hum, before a spray of discs were released on the back swing. Those with greater skill were able to effectively wield a lanvarok one-handed and in tandem with a blaster pistol. Lanvaroks were also on occasion used to pry open cargo bay [[Blast door/Legends|blast doors]]. The lanvarok's pointed summit kept enemies at bay under threat of impalement. When not in use, the lanvarok was worn in a [[Scabbard/Legends|scabbard]] across the back,<ref name="CC" /> or simply held in hand, ready for action.<ref name="TSW3">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 3|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 3]]</ref> Neither the polearm lanvarok<ref name="TSW5">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 5]]</ref> nor the discs with which it was equipped were able to withstand direct contact with a lightsaber's blade.<ref name="TSW2">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 2|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 2]]</ref>

[[File:NiceSwing.jpg|thumb|left|270px|A Massassi lanvarok in action]]
The gauntlet lanvarok design was inspired by the natural left-handedness of the Sith species. Although the primary release mechanism was located in the palm, the wielder enjoyed enough freedom to arm him- or herself with additional weapons in either hand. The subtle, [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force-activated]] trigger toward the forearm cuff made for unexpected discharges of the ammunition.<ref name="NEGWT" /> The tedious reload time was mitigated by the unpredictability of multiple discs, quietly dispersed in a short yet random and nearly inescapable spray; opponents were completely surprised<ref name="DSS" /> by a weapon that fired and dealt damage comparable to a blaster pistol.<ref name="KOTORCG" /> The cortosis-alloy that was occasionally incorporated in lanvarok construction was an added measure of protection from reciprocal lightsaber attacks.<ref name="NEGWT" /> Each weapon was designed specifically for the right or left hand without interchangeability.<ref name="DSS" />

==History==
{{Quote|If it has blood, you can make it bleed. If it has eyes, you can blind it. If it has a mouth, you can make it scream&hellip;|Inscription found on an ancient lanvarok|<ref name="NEGWT" />}}
Lanvaroks were in use by ancient Massassi warriors long before the arrival of the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[exiles]] of the [[Hundred-Year Darkness/Legends|Hundred-Year Darkness]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]] whose technological advancements brought an end to the primitive and barbarous culture of the Sith.<ref name="NEGWT" /> [[Sorzus Syn]], one of those same Dark Jedi who then became the first Sith Lords, recorded a description of both lanvarok versions within her [[Book of Sith|journal]], including her first encounter with the forearm mounted versions equipped by the [[Armor/Legends|armored]] [[Domoru Krev soldier|soldiers]] of [[Domoru Krev]].<ref name="BOS" /> Directions for the construction of Massassi lanvaroks were sometimes found within [[Sith holocron/Legends|Sith holocrons]]. Legend told that hunting was its primary purpose; by the [[Golden Age of the Sith|height]] of [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith civilization]], however, the lanvarok had been the Massassi's foremost combat weapon for generations. [[Marka Ragnos]], the immensely powerful [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] Golden Age, wielded a lanvarok, among other weapons, in battle.<ref name="DSS" /> Many of the Massassi warriors under the command of Ragnos' successor, [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]], were armed with lanvaroks as they invaded the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]].<ref name="FOTSE3" /> Among Sadow's [[Sith invasion fleet|forces]] was the [[Sith dreadnaught]] [[Harbinger (Sith dreadnaught)|''Harbinger'']], crewed by Massassi warriors who utilized lanvaroks to little effect&mdash;and often each other's bane&mdash;against the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] infiltrator [[Relin Druur]]. The surviving Massassi still wielded their lanvaroks against Druur when a botched [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jump resulted in the propulsion of the ''Harbinger'' [[41 ABY|several millennia]] into the future.<ref name="CC" /> Another Sith Dreadnaught, the ''[[Omen]]'', was said to have born resemblance to a lanvarok gauntlet.<ref name="LOTS8">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Secrets]]''</ref> While lanvaroks had been exposed to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large during the Hyperspace War, with the defeat and near-annihilation of the Sith Empire by war's end, they were anything but prevalent.<ref name="NEGWT" /> The device was still remembered by the citizens of the succeeding [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Empire]], whose Lords regarded lanvaroks with much admiration.<ref name="Deceived">''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]''</ref>

The remnants of the Massassi race relocated to the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] and maintained lanvarok usage for the duration of their existence. In [[3997 BBY]], descendants of the original colonists were visited by the Dark Jedi [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], whom they disarmed with discs hurled from polearm lanvaroks. When the Massassi later became subjects of Kun, who had since become Dark Lord of the Sith, they wielded lanvaroks in the pursuant [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. The signature polearm became something of a rarity with the eradication of the Massassi after the war,<ref name="DSS" /> and discovery of one usually fetched plentiful returns.<ref name="MR4" />

[[File:MaraArsenal.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Assassin Mara Jade eyes her arsenal of weapons, among them a wrist-mounted lanvarok]]
Forearm-mounted lanvarok gauntlets were seen in the galaxy following the institution of the [[Order of the Sith Lords]], but were still as uncommon as the polearm version. One of the final Lords of that Order, [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], armed himself with a lanvarok gauntlet.<ref name="SWDP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] owned a Sith lanvarok and contemplated its use for an [[Assassin/Legends|assassination]] attempt against the [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Dequc]]. However, its need for a left-handed operator ultimately forced Jade to choose another weapon.<ref name="MJ1">[[Mara Jade – By the Emperor's Hand 1|''Mara Jade – By the Emperor's Hand'' 1]]</ref> Jade then gave the lanvarok to her friend and [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Talon Karrde]],<ref name="IJ">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref> who tried to sell it to fellow privateer [[Booster Terrik]], much to the interest of his daughter [[Mirax Terrik Horn|Mirax]].<ref name="TBW">''[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]''</ref>

In [[5 ABY/Legends|5 ABY]], while in search of a rare lanvarok, [[Plumba]] of the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]] visited the [[Antiques by Dumas proprietor|proprietor]] of [[Antiques by Dumas]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Imperial Center]], who had recently acquired a priceless specimen. Plumba paid top dollar for the artifact,<ref name="MR4" /> only to die when he soon afterward activated the device,<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|31|Plumba}}</ref> a booby-trap set for him by [[Director of Imperial Intelligence|Imperial Intelligence Director]] [[Ysanne Isard]].<ref name="MR4" />

During the [[Second Galactic Civil War]], [[Padawan/Legends|Jedi apprentice]] [[Ben Skywalker]] experienced a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] of a female [[Sith Warrior]] armed with a Massassi lanvarok, a sighting that helped him learn to operate an ancient [[Sith Meditation Sphere]].<ref name="Exile">''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The Massassi lanvarok first appeared in [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith|''Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi - Dark Lords of the Sith'']]. The weapon was initially drawn by [[Chris Gossett]], with its last appearance in that story arc rendered by [[Art Wetherell]]. [[John Whitman]]'s [[Tales of the Jedi: Dark Lords of the Sith (audio drama)|audio rendition]] of ''Dark Lords of the Sith'', featured lanvaroks in action, complete with sound effects of the discharge of the weapon's discs. Carrasco returned as the penciller of [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'']], several issues of which featured polearm lanvarok-armed Massassi warriors. A lone Massassi lanvarok also appeared in [[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 3|''First Encounter'']], the third comic in [[Star Wars: Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'']] penciled by artist [[Dario Carrasco, Jr.]]. Lanvaroks and the unique fighting style employed by the Massassi were also featured prominently in author [[Paul S. Kemp]]'s ''[[Crosscurrent]]'', a novel set in the same [[Old Republic era|era]] as ''The Fall of the Sith Empire 3: First Encounter''. The weapon was also briefly mentioned in another of Kemp's works, ''[[The Old Republic: Deceived]]''.

The first appearance of an otherwise nondescript ''Sith'' lanvarok occurred in [[February]] of [[1997]], six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] before the [[August]] debut of the previously established Massassi version, in [[Michael A. Stackpole]]'s ''[[X-Wing: The Bacta War]]''. He purposely neglected to describe the weapon beyond its left-handed requirement, which resulted in a running gag, also of his design, about an interesting weapon that had yet to be visually depicted for fans.<ref name="Endnotes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2012/03/endnotes-for-star-wars-book-of-sith.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Book of Sith endnotes}}</ref> Stackpole's [[1998]] ''[[I, Jedi]]'' novel mentioned the lanvarok from ''The Bacta War'', and the same weapon was drawn several months later by [[Carlos Ezquerra]] for the [[Mara Jade – By the Emperor's Hand 1|first]] issue of the ''[[Star Wars: Mara Jade – By the Emperor's Hand]]'' comic book series. Mara Jade's lanvarok was again referenced in the [[Star Wars: Empire at War: Prima Official Game Guide|official video game game guide]] for ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]''. The weapon was briefly mentioned in the ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]] and appeared in [[Aaron Allston]]'s ''[[Legacy of the Force: Exile]]'' via Force vision.

Full specifications and historical data was given for both lanvarok versions, along with illustrations, in [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s [[The Dark Side Sourcebook|''Dark Side Sourcebook'']], with ''Sith'' used interchangeably to describe the two variations. Also, the forearm version rendered for the aforementioned source effectively put an end to Michael Stackpole's gag, and resulted in the retcon of the polearm as the prototype predecessor to the mounted launcher.<ref name="Endnotes" /> Additional details were provided [[2004|three years]] afterward in [[Del Rey]]'s [[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology|''New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology'']], which included a fully illustrated schematic of the forearm-mounted design, and also noted the polearm version's transition to a forearm-mounted weapon.

Although a Massassi lanvarok is shown releasing three simultaneous discs in [[Tales of the Jedi – Dark Lords of the Sith 4|''Dark Lords of the Sith 4: Death of a Dark Jedi'']], a description supported by ''The Dark Side Sourcebook'', Wizards of the Coast's ''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]'' describes instead a single discharge weapon. Visual depictions of both versions were provided in [[Drew Karpyshyn]]'s ''[[Heritage of the Sith]]'', an article for [[Star Wars Insider 88|''Star Wars Insider'' 88]], while a convoluted historical mention of the lanvarok was given in ''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties'', an online supplement to the same magazine. An entry was provided for only the forearm-mounted lanvarok in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', a reference book written by [[Stephen J. Sansweet]] and [[Pablo Hidalgo]]. Both lanvarok versions were referenced in [[2012]]'s ''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]'' reference book, in an in-universe account given by original Sith Lord Sorzus Syn.
